chapter: Don Redman's band at Connie's Inn
title: Connie's Inn: network broadcasts and the club
summary: Redman's band broadcast on CBS and WMCA; Jackson describes Connie's Inn, its floor show, owners and its location at 131st and Seventh Avenue.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That's right. And what a beautiful band. We used to broadcast over the network, CBS. We used to broadcast three times a week, sometimes four, over CBS and then every night we broadcasted over WMCA, every night. We got
What kind of club was that? Connie's Inn, Brother?

Connie's Inn was a nice little club. It had a show. It had a floor show just like -- but it wasn't as elaborate as the Cotton Club's show but it was a good floor show. It had chorus girls in it and comedians and singers, you know.
Connie Immerman was the guy that owned it, wasn't it? A little fat guy, Connie Immerman?
He had a brother, George Immerman.
On a corner of 131st and Seventh Avenue, downstairs.
The little awning is still out there.
Right, and you go down the steps.
Go down the basement. That's right. The Lafayette Theater was next door.
And it was a beautiful little club
